entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The instant bail application has been preferred by the petitioner for grant of regular bail for the offences registered under Sections 386/420/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, Sections 25(1-B)
a/26/35/31/25(6) of the Arms Act and Section 11 of the Bengal Public Gambling Act, 1867.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has falsely been implicated in this Ashish Mishra vs The State Of Jharkhand .......... Opp. ... on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121973925/
1 case and for no offence he is languishing in judicial custody since 29.10.2024 and the charge- sheet has already been submitted in this case.

entities.text: Ashish Mishra vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such he may be enlarged on bail.
4. Learned A.P.P. opposed the prayer for bail.
5. Having regard to the facts of the case and looking to the allegation made against this petitioner, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount 2025:JHHC:14657 each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Deoghar in connection with Deoghar (Town) P.S. Case No. 42 of 2023, corresponding to G.R. Case No. 406 of 2023.
6.

It is made clear that he shall appear on each and every date before the learned trial court and he shall not threaten any witness and shall co-operate in trial and if any adverse report will come against this petitioner, learned trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of this petitioner.
(Deepak Roshan, J.) Vikas/Arpit Ashish Mishra vs The State Of Jharkhand .......... Opp. ... on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121973925/
